newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks open easier on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks open easier on profit-taking.

text.p: * Toronto stocks dropped at Tuesday's open as investors took profits following three-day winning streak. * Eye on bank earnings. * 8.5 million shares traded worth C$117 million.
Toronto stocks slipped at Tuesday's open in thin trading as market players sold issues to reap rewards following three days of record closes.
"Everything's down slightly. We had a good run up yesterday," one trader said. "It's not unusual for people to want to lock in some profits."

Strength in key banks pushed Toronto to its 15th record close yesterday. Banks are seen gaining on the back of record quarterly earnings, starting today with the Bank of Montreal and the Bank of Nova Scotia. "That would be the group that would lead Toronto higher," the trader said.
Another trader said today's trading was quiet as market players were awaiting Friday's slew of U.S. economic data for more direction on inflation rates.
Except for golds, Toronto's 14 sub-sectors all lost ground led by consumer products, conglomerates, oils and banks.
Losing issues outpaced winners 243 to 170 while 243 traded flat.
* Royal Bank of Canada, Canada's largest bank, lost 1.10 to 60.60 in heavy trading following yesterday's gains.
* Hollinger Inc rose 0.05 to 11.35 in very light trading after posting first quarter per share earnings of C$2.73, after unusual items, compared to a year earlier C$0.05.
